speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with agitation and a yellowish discoloration of your skin and eyes, which suggests jaundice. To understand the cause, have you been experiencing any abdominal pain, fever, or changes in your urine or stool color recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Hepatitis B.

The patient's history of high-risk sexual behavior combined with the classic presentation of jaundice and agitation strongly suggests an acute viral hepatitis infection, specifically Hepatitis B, though Hepatitis A and C are also possibilities given his social history. Have you noticed any dark urine or pale stools, and do you have any memory gaps or confusion regarding recent events?
